01
The mysterious one / East Didsbury

Escape the Creepy Carnival

A spooky team challenge60-minute game

A fairground that comes alive after dark is an excellent setting for an escape-room challenge. At Houdini’s Creepy Carnival, the aim is not simply to open a few padlocks. Your group must work through a deliberately spooky story, gather objects, interpret clues and find a way out before the hour is up.

Houdini’s frames the game around a long-abandoned carnival and a fictional disappearance. Eerie music and performers are part of the experience, alongside puzzles that depend on people paying attention to different details. The attraction advertises live actors and unexpected scares, so this is one to choose deliberately, not a surprise booking for someone who dislikes horror.

The appeal is how quickly a group changes from curious spectators into a team. One person may spot a symbol while somebody else joins the dots; another keeps track of what has been tried. You do not need to know the answers in advance, and the best group discussion afterwards is about how you approached the challenge without giving its secrets away.

Why it’s worth going: Choose this if your group wants a shared story, a little fear and something to talk about afterwards.

Try thisBefore entering, agree who will keep an eye on the time, who likes visual clues and who enjoys word or number puzzles. Roles can change once the game begins. Afterwards, compare which kind of clue helped you move forward.

Make the adventure happen

01

Choose the right game

Book Creepy Carnival specifically at Houdini’s, within Tenpin at Parrs Wood. The operator accepts groups of two to eight.

02

Check the scare and age rules

It features live actors. Players aged 12–16 need a paying adult in the game; older teenagers have separate supervision and waiver conditions.

03

Compare the real total

The advertised £75 Wednesday deal covers up to six players only with code MIDBREAK, subject to exclusions and availability. Other dates and group sizes vary.

04

Keep the surprises intact

After the game, discuss your teamwork without spoiling the puzzles for a future group.

02
The curious one / Hulme

Rescue the Mad Hatter’s guests

An imaginative family quest75-minute adventure

A tea party is ready, but its guests have vanished. In this Z-arts experience, your group steps into a theatrical Wonderland environment and sets off with a digital tablet. The mission is to follow a trail of clues and bring the missing characters back before the seventy-five minutes run out.

It is part escape-room puzzle, part scavenger hunt and part interactive game. Instead of sitting through a show, you explore the environment, handle challenges and decide what each new clue means. Z-arts says you meet the Mad Hatter by the riverbank at the start, and other teams may be exploring the wider space at the same time while following their own route.

The experience is designed for families, but it does not require the adults to pretend they are merely accompanying the children. Spotting visual details, remembering story fragments and testing theories are all useful. A mixed-age group can play to different strengths, which makes the adventure particularly appealing for an unusual family celebration.

Why it’s worth going: Choose this for an imaginative family challenge that needs cooperation rather than competitive speed.

Try thisLet a different person lead each stage: clue hunter, tablet navigator, story detective and final decision-maker. See whether the person who notices the most details is also the person who solves the final riddle.

Make the adventure happen

01

Book the exact experience

Select Mission: Mad Hatter rather than the separate general Adventures in Wonderland visit.

02

Bring the right team

The normal format is three to six players with at least one adult. It is designed for ages 9+, although Z-arts allows children aged 7+ in family teams.

03

Follow the clues

Collect the tablet, explore the decorated space and solve a mix of physical and digital puzzles.

04

Make it a whole outing

Allow time to get into Hulme and meet the booked start time. Ask Z-arts about accessibility adaptations before purchasing.

03
The fast one / East Manchester

Ride a flying lap in a real velodrome

Track cycling, coached90-minute coached experience

The banked curves of Manchester’s National Cycling Centre look very different from an ordinary cycle path. The experience offers the chance to try a proper fixed-wheel track bike inside a purpose-built velodrome, under the direction of an instructor, rather than watching the action from the stands.

Your session starts with fitting equipment and learning the basics. You watch a briefing, meet the coach and get accustomed to the track bike before progressing around the banking. The aim is to build control and confidence, not to pretend you have suddenly become a professional racer. That distinction matters: a normal cyclist can be new to velodrome riding, but cannot be new to riding a bicycle altogether.

The finale is a timed flying lap, which gives the experience a satisfying finish. There is something unusually memorable about seeing the track from a rider’s perspective and then having a real number to take home. It is also a strong choice for somebody who enjoys skill-based challenges more than rides or passive attractions.

Why it’s worth going: Choose this if you want an achievable first-timer challenge with a distinctive sporting finish.

Try thisPay attention to one technical detail your coach teaches, perhaps how you look through a corner or how a fixed-wheel bike feels. Afterwards, write down your lap time and what made the banking easier to understand.

Make the adventure happen

01

Choose the correct booking

Book the National Cycling Centre’s Velodrome Experience, not a separate accreditation or BMX session.

02

Check your suitability

You must be at least 12 years old, at least 145 cm tall and able to ride an ordinary two-wheeled bike unaided.

03

Learn from the coach

The organiser supplies a track bike, helmet and cleated shoes. It begins with fitting and safety instruction.

04

Finish with the flying lap

The 90-minute session builds towards a timed lap. Book a suitable available date and follow the instructor’s directions throughout.

04
The outdoors one / Heaton Mersey → Northenden

Kayak the Mersey and tackle the waterslide

River adventure · seasonalAbout 1–1½ hours on the water, plus briefing and independent return journey.

The Mersey is an unlikely place to picture a mini-expedition. Yet Venture Out’s Short Splash turns a stretch of river between Heaton Mersey and Northenden into a memorable adventure, with shallow rapids early on, river bends to negotiate and a waterslide weir near the finish.

The operator describes a 5.5 km trip that takes roughly one to one-and-a-half hours on the water. You can book an eligible self-guided sit-on-top kayak or ask about guided options with other craft. There is a briefing and safety equipment; which conditions and routes are appropriate are decisions for the operator, not for a reader to judge from an illustration.

An important practical detail makes this a proper point-to-point outing: the company collects its boats at Northenden, but it does not transport the people back to Heaton Mersey. That means arranging a lift, leaving a suitable car at the finish or organising a taxi before you set off. A spare change of clothes is sensible, and the launch and exit may involve steps. Plan it for the usual April-to-September season rather than treating it as an autumn drop-in.

Why it’s worth going: Choose this for an outdoors challenge that feels much further from the city than it actually is, provided you book an appropriate operator-run trip.

Try thisMake the logistics part of the adventure. Before booking, work out who is travelling with you, where you will finish, how you will return and what dry clothes you will need. Then let the organiser judge whether the river is suitable on your chosen day.

Make the adventure happen

01

Save it for the right season

Regular public river dates normally run weekends April–September. Contact Venture Out about other dates, which may be possible by arrangement.

02

Choose the right craft

The operator lists £20 for an adult self-guided single sit-on-top kayak to Northenden; check current prices, other craft and eligibility.

03

Listen to the river briefing

The route includes bends and the operator’s described waterslide weir. River levels can change the trip or cause postponement.

04

Arrange your own return

The Short Splash finishes at Riverside Park, Northenden. Venture Out collects boats, not passengers. Arrange transport before starting.

The practical details

Where
Heaton Mersey → Northenden
Time
About 1–1½ hours on the water, plus briefing and independent return journey.
Cost
Officially listed at £20 for an adult, self-guided single sit-on-top kayak to Northenden; other options cost more.
Best for
Adults and families who are comfortable following water-safety guidance; suitability depends on craft, ability and river conditions.
When
Regular trips on weekends April–September; other dates by arrangement.

Before you bookSEASONAL: regular trips April–September, other dates by arrangement. River levels may lead to changes or cancellation. Wear the required buoyancy aid and helmet, and discuss any medical, swimming or accessibility needs with the operator. The illustrated river is not a navigational or safety guide.

Useful, exciting and properly checked.

This is an independent editorial guide, not a booking service. Each featured experience is real, but sessions, age conditions, prices and river conditions change. The information was checked against organiser pages on 28 October 2026. The guide does not claim anyone on the Radar team has personally completed the activities.

The illustrations are original conceptual artwork. They are not venue photographs, evidence of exact layouts or safe navigation instructions. Use the linked official websites for current details.

Special note on the river trip: regular public dates are normally April–September; outside that period dates are by arrangement. It is a point-to-point activity and Venture Out does not return passengers to the start.

About the reward: This four-adventure edition is the current South Manchester Radar referral reward for one eligible new reader. It is a standalone collection; a longer edition is not promised.
